question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
I had never saw/ such a sight/ before I visited Switzerland.
options: such a sight
No error
before I visited Switzerland.
I had never saw
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "I had never saw"


Explanation:

☛The phrase "I had never saw" in the given sentence is incorrect.
☛Here, Past Perfect Tense is used, which requires the third form of the verb (Past Participle) after "had".
☛"Saw" is the second form of the verb, while "seen" is the third form.
☛The correct phrase should be: "I had never seen".



Grammar Rules:

☛In Past Perfect Tense, we use had + V3 (Past Participle).
☛Verb Forms: Base Form (V1) - see, Past Simple (V2) - saw, Past Participle (V3) - seen.
☛Past Perfect is used to show that one action in the past was completed before another action in the past.



Example:
InCorrect - I had never saw such a sight before.

Correct - I had never seen such a sight before.

Explanation:

☛दिए गए वाक्य में "I had never saw" एक गलत वाक्यांश है।
☛यहाँ Past Perfect Tense का प्रयोग किया गया है, जिसमें "had" के बाद Verb की Third Form (Past Participle) का प्रयोग होता है।
☛"Saw" Verb की Second Form है, जबकि "seen" इसकी Third Form है।
☛सही वाक्यांश होना चाहिए: "I had never seen"।



Grammar Rules:

☛Past Perfect Tense में had + V3 (Past Participle) का प्रयोग होता है।
☛क्रिया की Forms: Base Form (V1) - see, Past Simple (V2) - saw, Past Participle (V3) - seen।
☛Past Perfect का प्रयोग अतीत में एक कार्य के पूरा होने के बाद दूसरे कार्य के होने को दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है।



Example:
InCorrect - I had never saw such a sight before.

Correct - I had never seen such a sight before.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
Ravi said that / his red jacket is / the cheaper than all other jackets.
options: the cheaper than all other jackets.
his red jacket is
No error
Ravi said that
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "the cheaper than all other jackets."


Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the part "the cheaper than all other jackets".
☛ Here, "cheaper" (comparative degree) is used, but the use of "the" before it is incorrect because "the" is used with comparative degree only when comparing two things and the sentence has a clue like "of the two".
☛ The correct sentence should be: "cheaper than all other jackets" (without "the") because the comparison is being made among multiple jackets.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Degree is used to compare two things.
☛ If the comparison is among more than two things, "the" is not used.
☛ Superlative Degree always uses "the", e.g., "the cheapest of all jackets".


Example:
InCorrect - This is the better than all other options.
Correct - This is better than all other options.
question_hi:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
Ravi said that / his red jacket is / the cheaper than all other jackets.
options_hi: the cheaper than all other jackets.
his red jacket is
No error
Ravi said that
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "the cheaper than all other jackets."


Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "the cheaper than all other jackets" भाग में त्रुटि है।
☛ यहाँ "cheaper" (तुलनात्मक डिग्री) का प्रयोग किया गया है, लेकिन इसके पहले "the" का प्रयोग गलत है क्योंकि तुलनात्मक डिग्री के साथ "the" का प्रयोग तभी किया जाता है जब दो चीजों की तुलना की जा रही हो और वाक्य में "of the two" जैसा कोई संकेत हो।
☛ सही वाक्य होगा: "cheaper than all other jackets" (बिना "the" के) क्योंकि यहाँ कई जैकेट्स की तुलना की जा रही है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ तुलनात्मक डिग्री (Comparative Degree) का प्रयोग दो चीजों की तुलना करने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ यदि तुलना दो से अधिक चीजों के बीच हो, तो "the" का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता।
☛ Superlative Degree (सर्वोत्तम डिग्री) में हमेशा "the" का प्रयोग किया जाता है, जैसे: "the cheapest of all jackets"।


Example:
InCorrect - This is the better than all other options.
Correct - This is better than all other options.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
options: attends court
always looks in the
case before he
A good lawyer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "always looks in the"


Explanation:

☛The segment 'always looks in the' contains the error in the given sentence.
☛It should be 'always looks into the' because 'look into' is a phrasal verb meaning 'to investigate' or 'examine carefully'.
☛'look in' is incorrect here as it means 'to glance inside', which doesn't fit the context of examining a case.
☛This is a common error of wrong preposition usage with verbs.



Grammar Rules:

☛Phrasal Verbs: Small prepositions (in, into, on, at etc.) when combined with verbs often change their meaning completely, forming phrasal verbs.
☛Preposition Choice: 'Into' implies movement or transformation while 'in' suggests position or location.
☛Exam Focus: Competitive exams frequently test knowledge of phrasal verbs and correct preposition usage.



Example:
InCorrect - The committee will look in the complaint.

Correct - The committee will look into the complaint.
question_hi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

options_hi: attends court
always looks in the
case before he
A good lawyer
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "always looks in the"


Explanation:

☛दिए गए वाक्य में 'always looks in the' खंड में गलती है।
☛सही वाक्यांश होना चाहिए 'always looks into the' क्योंकि 'look into' एक phrasal verb है जिसका अर्थ है 'जांच करना' या 'विस्तार से देखना'।
☛'look in' का प्रयोग गलत है क्योंकि इसका अर्थ होता है 'अंदर देखना', जो इस संदर्भ में उचित नहीं है।
☛यहाँ preposition का गलत प्रयोग हुआ है, जो एक सामान्य grammatical error है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Phrasal Verbs: कई बार छोटे prepositions (in, into, on, at आदि) का प्रयोग verb के साथ मिलकर अर्थ बदल देता है। इन्हें phrasal verbs कहते हैं।
☛Preposition Usage: Prepositions का चुनाव context पर निर्भर करता है। 'Into' movement दर्शाता है जबकि 'in' स्थिति दर्शाता है।
☛Common Error: Competitive exams में अक्सर phrasal verbs और preposition के गलत प्रयोग पर questions पूछे जाते हैं।



Example:
InCorrect - She looked in the matter carefully.

Correct - She looked into the matter carefully.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.
Jack along with / his family visited / his aunt living / at America.
options: Jack along with
his family visited
his aunt living
at America
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "at America"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "at America" is incorrect because the preposition 'at' is used for smaller or specific locations (e.g., home, school), while 'in' is used for larger areas like countries.
☛ The correct preposition for countries is 'in'. Thus, the sentence should be: "Jack along with his family visited his aunt living in America."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Preposition 'in' vs 'at':
- Use 'in' for large places (countries, cities).
- Use 'at' for small or specific places (home, station).
☛ Examples:
- InCorrect: He works at Canada.
- Correct: He works in Canada.

solution_hi:

Explanation:

☛ 'At' का उपयोग छोटे स्थानों (जैसे घर, स्कूल) के लिए किया जाता है, जबकि 'in' बड़े क्षेत्रों (देश, शहर) के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ सही वाक्य होगा: "Jack along with his family visited his aunt living in America."

- 'At' का प्रयोग छोटे या विशिष्ट स्थानों (घर, पार्क, स्टेशन) के लिए होता है।
☛ Examples:
- InCorrect: She lives at India.
- Correct: She lives in India.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
His skills in programming / are more superior than / most developers / in the company.
options: most developers
in the company
are more superior than
His skills in programming
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "are more superior than"


Explanation:

☛The segment "are more superior than" contains a grammatical error.
☛The word "superior" itself carries a comparative meaning, so using "more" with it is redundant.
☛The correct phrase should be "are superior to" because "superior" is always followed by the preposition "to", not "than".
☛Here, "superior" is an adjective that is already in the comparative degree, so it should not be used with additional comparative words like "more".



Grammar Rules:

☛Comparative Adjectives: Some adjectives already have a comparative or superlative meaning, such as "superior", "inferior", "senior", and "junior". These should not be used with "more" or "most".
☛Prepositions: "Superior", "inferior", "senior", and "junior" are always followed by the preposition "to", not "than".
☛Double Comparison: Avoid using two comparative forms with the same adjective (e.g., "more better", "more superior", etc.).



Example:
InCorrect - His skills are more superior than others.

Correct - His skills are superior to others.

solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "are more superior than"


Explanation:

☛वाक्य में "are more superior than" एक व्याकरणिक त्रुटि है।
☛"Superior" शब्द पहले से ही तुलनात्मक अर्थ रखता है, इसलिए इसके साथ "more" का प्रयोग अनावश्यक है।
☛सही वाक्यांश होना चाहिए "are superior to" क्योंकि "superior" के साथ "to" preposition का प्रयोग होता है, "than" का नहीं।
☛यहाँ "superior" एक adjective है जो कि पहले से ही comparative degree में है, इसलिए इसके साथ और comparative degree के शब्दों का प्रयोग नहीं होना चाहिए।



Grammar Rules:

☛Comparative Adjectives: कुछ adjectives पहले से ही comparative या superlative अर्थ रखते हैं, जैसे "superior", "inferior", "senior", "junior"। इनके साथ "more" या "most" का प्रयोग नहीं होता।
☛Prepositions: "Superior", "inferior", "senior", और "junior" के साथ हमेशा "to" preposition का प्रयोग होता है, "than" का नहीं।
☛Double Comparison: एक ही adjective के साथ दो बार comparative degree का प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिए (जैसे "more better", "more superior" आदि)।



Example:
InCorrect - His skills are more superior than others.

Correct - His skills are superior to others.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the segment with the grammatical error.
I was surprised / to see my / daughter, Manya, riding her / new bicycle confident.
options: daughter, Manya, riding her
I was surprised
to see my
new bicycle confident
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "new bicycle confident"


Explanation:

☛The segment 'new bicycle confident' contains the grammatical error in the given sentence.
☛Here, 'confident' is an adjective that describes 'Manya' (noun), not the 'bicycle'.
☛Therefore, the correct sentence structure should be 'new bicycle confidently' because the adverb 'confidently' should be used to modify the verb 'riding'.
☛An adjective ('confident') is used to describe a noun or pronoun, while an adverb ('confidently') is used to modify a verb, adjective, or another adverb.



Grammar Rules:

☛Adjective vs Adverb: An adjective describes a noun or pronoun, while an adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
☛To form an adverb from an adjective, the suffix '-ly' is often added (e.g., confident → confidently).
☛Using the correct modifier in a sentence is crucial to ensure clarity of meaning.



Example:
InCorrect - She sings beautiful.

Correct - She sings beautifully.

options_hi: daughter, Manya, riding her

solution_hi:

Explanation:

☛यहाँ 'confident' एक adjective है जो कि 'Manya' (संज्ञा) को describe कर रहा है, न कि 'bicycle' को।
☛इसलिए, सही वाक्य रचना होनी चाहिए 'new bicycle confidently' क्योंकि यहाँ 'riding' (क्रिया) को modify करने के लिए adverb 'confidently' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛Adjective ('confident') का प्रयोग केवल संज्ञा या सर्वनाम को describe करने के लिए होता है, जबकि adverb ('confidently') का प्रयोग क्रिया, adjective या दूसरे adverb को modify करने के लिए होता है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Adjective vs Adverb: Adjective संज्ञा या सर्वनाम की विशेषता बताता है, जबकि Adverb क्रिया, adjective या दूसरे adverb की विशेषता बताता है।
☛Adjective का रूप बदलकर Adverb बनाने के लिए अक्सर '-ly' प्रत्यय जोड़ा जाता है (जैसे: confident → confidently)।
☛वाक्य में modifier का सही प्रयोग करना अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है ताकि अर्थ स्पष्ट रहे।



Example:
InCorrect - She sings beautiful.

Correct - She sings beautifully.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Sushil, who recently joined our school / was awarded the Gold Cup / as he worked hardly / throughout the year.
options: as he worked hardly
was awarded the Gold Cup
throughout the year.
Sushil, who recently joined our school
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "as he worked hardly"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the use of the word 'hardly'.
☛ 'Hardly' means 'scarcely' or 'almost not', which does not fit the context here.
☛ The correct word should be 'hard', meaning 'with great effort'.
☛ Thus, the correct phrase should be: "as he worked hard".

Grammar Rules:
☛ 'Hard' can function as both an adjective and an adverb, whereas 'hardly' is only an adverb.
☛ 'Hard' is used to describe physical or mental effort.
☛ 'Hardly' is used to indicate scarcity or negation (e.g., "I hardly know him").

Example:
InCorrect - She ran hardly in the race.
Correct - She ran hard in the race.

options_hi: as he worked hardly
was awarded the Gold Cup
throughout the year.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
☛ इस वाक्य में 'hardly' शब्द का प्रयोग गलत है।
☛ 'Hardly' का अर्थ है 'मुश्किल से' या 'बहुत कम', जो यहाँ अर्थ के अनुसार उचित नहीं है।
☛ सही शब्द 'hard' होना चाहिए, जिसका अर्थ है 'कठिन परिश्रम'।
☛ इस प्रकार, सही वाक्यांश होगा: "as he worked hard"।

Grammar Rules:

☛ 'Hard' का प्रयोग physical or mental effort (शारीरिक या मानसिक परिश्रम) को दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ 'Hardly' का प्रयोग scarcely (बहुत कम) या almost not (लगभग नहीं) के अर्थ में किया जाता है।

Example:

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
Playing in the field, the young gayer students were laughing and giggling.
options: gay
more gay
gayest
most gay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "gay"


Explanation:
☛ The word 'gayer' is incorrect in this sentence because it describes a general characteristic (gay) of the students, and there is no need for a comparative or superlative form here.
☛ 'gay' is an adjective that simply describes the happiness of the students without any comparison.
☛ Comparative and superlative forms are used only when comparing two or more things or people. There is no such context here.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Positive Degree: When an adjective is used to describe a noun or pronoun without any comparison, it is called the Positive Degree. Example: She is happy.
☛ Comparative Degree: When two persons or things are compared, the Comparative Degree is used. Example: She is happier than her sister.
☛ Superlative Degree: When more than two persons or things are compared to show the highest or lowest degree, the Superlative Degree is used. Example: She is the happiest girl in the class.


Example:
InCorrect - The young gayer students were laughing.
Correct - The young gay students were laughing.
question_hi:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
Playing in the field, the young gayer students were laughing and giggling.
options_hi: gay
more gay
gayest
most gay
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "gay"


Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में 'gayer' शब्द का प्रयोग गलत है क्योंकि यहाँ विद्यार्थियों की एक सामान्य विशेषता (gay) का वर्णन किया जा रहा है, तुलनात्मक (comparative) या अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण (superlative) रूप की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
☛ 'gay' एक विशेषण (adjective) है जो यहाँ बिना किसी तुलना के विद्यार्थियों की प्रसन्नता को दर्शाता है।
☛ तुलनात्मक (comparative) और अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण (superlative) रूपों का प्रयोग तभी किया जाता है जब दो या अधिक वस्तुओं या व्यक्तियों की तुलना की जाती है। यहाँ ऐसा कोई संदर्भ नहीं है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ Positive Degree: जब किसी विशेषण का प्रयोग बिना किसी तुलना के किसी संज्ञा या सर्वनाम की विशेषता बताने के लिए किया जाता है, तो उसे Positive Degree कहते हैं। उदाहरण: She is happy.
☛ Comparative Degree: जब दो व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं की तुलना की जाती है, तो Comparative Degree का प्रयोग किया जाता है। उदाहरण: She is happier than her sister.

question:

options: she forbade

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "him not"


Explanation:
• In the given sentence "She forbade him not to enter that room.", the segment "him not" is incorrect.
• The correct structure for "forbid" is "forbid + object + to + verb", not "forbid + object + not + to + verb".
• Since "forbid" itself means "to order someone not to do something", using "not" with it creates redundancy and is grammatically wrong.
• The correct sentence should be: "She forbade him to enter that room."


Grammar Rules:
• Forbid is used as "forbid + object + to + verb" (Example: She forbade him to leave.)
• Prohibit is used as "prohibit + object + from + verb+ing" (Example: She prohibited him from leaving.)
• "Not" should not be used with "forbid" as it already carries a negative meaning.


Example:
InCorrect - She forbade him not to attend the party.
Correct - She forbade him to attend the party.
